mainTopic: The three things to cling to and to avoid, the meaning of תוקע עצמו לדבר הלכה, and רבן גמליאל's reason about a minor's קידושין and her sister the יבמה.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining a ברייתא about three things to cling to and three things to stay away from. רבי אבהו shows from the word 'pursue' that pursuing peace is a great מצוה. רבי נתן's teaching explains why annulling vows is praised. Next the גמרא gives a short reason for avoiding מיאונין, פקדונות from a fellow townsman, and ערבי שלציון. רבי יצחק reads a פסוק as warning about those who accept converts, ערבי שלציון, and one who is תוקע עצמו לדבר הלכה. The גמרא explains that last phrase in several ways: through רבי יוסי's teaching about Torah without doing, or as a judge who compares cases instead of asking his teacher. Then the גמרא returns to the משנה and asks רב for רבן גמליאל's reason. רב answers that the minor's קידושין become complete only after relations once she is an adult. רב ששת challenges this, רבין defends it, and the גמרא then points to another ruling of רב that seems to contradict it. The discussion of that contradiction continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Pursuing peace is learned from the word 'pursue'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו shows through a גזירה שוה that pursuing peace is a great מצוה, just like pursuing צדקה and חסד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: we learn it from the word 'pursue' appearing in two places. Here it says 'Seek peace and pursue it,' and there it says 'One who pursues righteousness and kindness will find life, righteousness and honor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still explaining why the ברייתא tells us to cling to making peace. רבי אבהו gives a source from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'pursue' appears both about peace and about צדקה וחסד. Through a גזירה שוה, the great reward promised to one who pursues צדקה וחסד also applies to one who pursues peace.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there (the setup of a גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abahu said:
It is learned from 'pursuit' and 'pursuit.'
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word in two פסוקים links their meaning together.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'Seek peace and pursue it,'
and it is written there: 'One who pursues righteousness and kindness
will find life, righteousness, and honor.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אָתְיָא רְדִיפָה רְדִיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of 'making peace' from the ברייתא, which was discussed just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pursuing peace earns the same great reward as pursuing צדקה וחסד, learned through a גזירה שוה on the word 'pursue.'

steps.title: Annulling vows is good, following רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא praises annulling vows because, according to רבי נתן, making a vow is like building a private altar, and keeping it is like bringing a קרבן on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Annulling vows follows רבי נתן. It was taught: רבי נתן says, one who makes a vow is as if he built a private altar, and one who keeps the vow is as if he offered a sacrifice on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third thing to cling to, annulling vows. It ties it to a ברייתא of רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building a private במה after the בית המקדש is forbidden. רבי נתן compares a vow to building one, and keeping the vow to using it. So it is better to have the vow undone than to keep it.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar, forbidden outside the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The three things to cling to are now explained: חליצה, pursuing peace (רבי אבהו), and annulling vows (רבי נתן).

phrases.english: Annulling vows follows Rabbi Natan.
As it was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
One who vows is as if he built a private altar.
And one who keeps it is as if he offered a sacrifice on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the second item in the ברייתא (peace) to the third (annulling vows).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vows are viewed negatively, so undoing them is praised, following רבי נתן.

steps.title: Stay away from refusals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists three things to avoid. The first is מיאון, because the girl may grow up and regret refusing her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one should stay away from three things: from refusals, because perhaps she will grow up and regret it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second half of the ברייתא, the three things to avoid, and explains the first one: מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl married off as a minor can leave the marriage through מיאון. A רב should avoid arranging this, because once she is older she may regret leaving a husband who was good for her.

keyTerms.meaning: Refusals: a minor girl leaving a marriage her family arranged

phrases.english: And one should distance himself from three things:
From refusals,
perhaps she will grow up and regret it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the three things to cling to over to the three things to avoid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid involvement in מיאון, since the girl may later regret it.

steps.title: Stay away from deposits from a fellow townsman
steps.stepSummary: Avoid taking a פקדון from someone in your own town, since he treats your house like his own and may take it without telling you.
steps.simpleTranslation: From deposits: this means from a person of the same town, because he treats your house like his own house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second thing to avoid: guarding deposits, and narrows it to deposits from a neighbor in the same town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone from your own town comes in and out of your home freely. He might take his deposit back without your knowledge and later claim you lost it, so the guardian could be wrongly blamed.

keyTerms.meaning: Deposits, items given to someone to guard
A person of the same town

phrases.english: From deposits: with a man of the same town,
since the guardian's house is like his own house to him.
phrases.notes: The first 'his house' is the guardian's house, and the second is the owner's own house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in the list of three things to avoid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The warning about deposits applies to deposits from someone of the same town.

steps.title: Stay away from a special kind of guarantee
steps.stepSummary: The warning about ערבון refers only to a ערב שלציון, a guarantor the lender may collect from directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: From guaranteeing: this refers to ערבי שלציון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third thing to avoid, being a guarantor, and limits it to one specific type of guarantee.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every guarantee is discouraged, only ערבי שלציון. With this kind, the lender can go straight to the guarantor to collect. The next steps bring a source and explain the name.

keyTerms.meaning: Being a guarantor for someone's loan
A type of guarantor the lender can collect from directly

phrases.english: From guaranteeing: with Sheltziyon guarantors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third item in the list of three things to avoid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The warning about guaranteeing refers specifically to ערבי שלציון.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: evil after evil for three types of people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads the פסוק 'רע ירוע כי ערב זר' as warning of trouble for those who accept converts, ערבי שלציון, and one who is תוקע עצמו לדבר הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק said: What is the meaning of 'He who guarantees for a stranger will surely suffer harm'? Evil after evil will come to those who accept converts, to ערבי שלציון, and to one who pushes himself into a matter of הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the warning about ערבי שלציון from רבי יצחק. He lists three kinds of people who will have trouble, and the next steps explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק reads the double wording 'רע ירוע' as 'evil after evil.' He reads 'ערב' as pointing to guarantors, and 'זר' (stranger) as hinting at converts. The ערבי שלציון from the ברייתא are one of the three groups.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written
One who pushes himself into matters of הלכה

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי דִּכְתִיב: ״רַע יֵרוֹעַ כִּי עָרַב זָר״ —
phrases.english: What is meant by what is written: 'He who guarantees for a stranger will surely suffer harm'?
Evil after evil will come
to those who accept converts, and to Sheltziyon guarantors,
and to one who pushes himself into a matter of halakha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source supporting the warning against ערבי שלציון from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That one should stay away from ערבי שלציון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק's reading of משלי 11:15, 'רע ירוע כי ערב זר.'

steps.title: Accepting converts follows רבי חלבו
steps.stepSummary: The trouble for those who accept converts is explained through רבי חלבו: converts are as hard for ישראל as a skin affliction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those who accept converts follows רבי חלבו, as רבי חלבו said: converts are as hard for ישראל as a ספחת on the skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the three groups from רבי יצחק's list, starting with those who accept converts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חלבו compares converts to a ספחת, a kind of צרעת mark on the skin. That is why one who accepts them is warned about trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of צרעת mark on the skin

phrases.english: Those who accept converts: this follows Rabbi Chelbo.
As Rabbi Chelbo said:
Converts are as difficult for Israel as a leprous sore on the skin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first group in רבי יצחק's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Accepting converts brings trouble because, per רבי חלבו, converts are hard for ישראל like a ספחת.

steps.title: What ערבי שלציון do
steps.stepSummary: ערבי שלציון are explained as 'pull out, thrust in': the borrower is pulled out and the guarantor is pushed into his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: ערבי שלציון: they practice 'pull out, thrust in.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second group: ערבי שלציון, and why their name fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name שלציון sounds like 'שלוף דוץ,' pull out and push in. The lender skips the borrower and goes straight to the guarantor, which is why this guarantee is so risky.

phrases.english: Sheltziyon guarantors: because they practice 'pull out, thrust in.'
phrases.notes: The borrower is pulled out of the picture, and the guarantor is pushed in to pay the loan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second group in רבי יצחק's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ערב שלציון is one the lender collects from in place of the borrower.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: one who says he has no Torah
steps.stepSummary: The third group, תוקע עצמו לדבר הלכה, is explained with רבי יוסי's ברייתא: one who says he has no Torah has no Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who pushes himself into a matter of הלכה: as it was taught, רבי יוסי says, anyone who says he has no Torah, has no Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third group using a ברייתא of רבי יוסי. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance, רבי יוסי seems to say only that a person who claims to have no Torah really does not have it. The גמרא will immediately ask what this adds.

phrases.english: One who pushes himself into a matter of halakha:
As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר אֵין לוֹ תּוֹרָה — אֵין לוֹ תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: Anyone who says he has no Torah has no Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹקֵעַ עַצְמוֹ לִדְבַר הֲלָכָה — דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third group in רבי יצחק's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי's ברייתא, as first quoted: one who says he has no Torah has no Torah.

steps.title: That is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if someone has no Torah, of course he has no Torah. Why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי יוסי's ברייתא as saying something too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teaching should tell us something new. 'He who has no Torah has no Torah' adds nothing, so the wording cannot be right as it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's statement 'כל האומר אין לו תורה אין לו תורה.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The statement adds nothing new, since it simply repeats itself.

steps.title: Corrected reading: one who has only Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: anyone who says he has nothing but Torah has nothing but Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: anyone who says he has nothing except Torah, has nothing except Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by rereading רבי יוסי's words so that they teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reading is about a person who claims his life is only Torah. He ends up with only Torah and nothing else. This explains the 'תוקע עצמו לדבר הלכה' in רבי יצחק's list.
steps.whatToRemember: The three things to avoid are מיאונין, פקדונות from a townsman, and ערבי שלציון. רבי יצחק warns about three groups: those who accept converts, ערבי שלציון, and one who is תוקע עצמו לדבר הלכה. The next steps keep working out what that last phrase means.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. The first one ('has no Torah') was rejected as obvious. This new reading ('has nothing except Torah') is also challenged in step 12, and steps 13–16 give two different answers.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: Rather: anyone who says he has nothing except Torah
has nothing except Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 10 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrected reading of the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי said that one who claims to have no Torah has no Torah, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי meant that one who claims to have only Torah ends up with only Torah, which explains 'תוקע עצמו לדבר הלכה.'

steps.title: The corrected reading is also obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the new reading from step 11 is also obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. Saying that someone who claims only Torah has only Torah also seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 changed the wording to 'he has nothing but Torah', meaning he gets reward only for learning. But that is plain: nobody gets reward for מצוות he never did. So the same problem from step 10 comes back.

phrases.english: This too is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the corrected wording given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'one who says he has nothing but Torah has nothing but Torah'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Of course he gets no reward for מצוות he did not do, so the statement would teach nothing new.

steps.title: He does not even have Torah
steps.stepSummary: The statement means that such a person does not even get credit for his Torah learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means that he does not even have Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי is teaching something stronger. A person who only learns and does not do does not even have the Torah he learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that learning without doing is not counted as Torah learning at all. That is far from obvious, so the statement is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not even have Torah

phrases.english: Rather, that he does not even have Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation that makes the statement teach a new point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought he at least gets credit for his learning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without doing, even his learning does not count.

steps.title: Why does his learning not count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source or reason behind the new reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next step by asking why learning without doing would not count as learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question, not an attack. It looks for the basis of the strong claim made in step 13.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the answer in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that learning without doing does not count.

steps.title: Learning and doing go together
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from the פסוק 'ולמדתם ועשיתם' that whoever is not doing is not counted as learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The פסוק says, 'You shall learn them and do them.' Whoever is part of doing is part of learning; whoever is not part of doing is not part of learning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a פסוק that puts learning and doing side by side. He learns from it that the two are tied together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the Torah joins 'learn' with 'do', learning that has no plan to do is not the learning the Torah means. This is the reason given for step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall learn them and do them

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source that Torah learning is meant to lead to action.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The verse says: “You shall learn them and do them” —
whoever is part of doing is part of learning,
whoever is not part of doing is not part of learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ties learning to doing, so learning without doing does not count.

steps.title: No reward even when others act on his teaching
steps.stepSummary: A second answer keeps the reading of step 11 and says it teaches that he gets no reward for מצוות others do because of his teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or say: really it is as you said at first, 'Whoever says he has nothing but Torah has nothing but Torah.' It is needed for a case where he teaches others and they go and do. You might think he gets reward for that, so it teaches us he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the objection in step 12. It keeps the earlier reading and shows a case where it teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is obvious he gets no reward for his own missing מצוות. The new point is about students who do מצוות because of his teaching: we might think he shares in their reward, but he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (a second answer)
It is needed only for (a special case)
You might have said... so it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is a second, separate answer to the objection of step 12, standing next to the answer of steps 13–15.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
really it is as you said at first:
phrases.notes: This points back to the reading from step 11.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: whoever says he has nothing but Torah —
has nothing but Torah,
it is needed only where he teaches others
and they go and do.
You might have said:
he himself has reward for it,
so it teaches us he does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 12, different from steps 13–15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the statement to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He might get reward when his students do מצוות because of his teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: He gets no reward even for that.

steps.title: A judge who compares cases instead of asking
steps.stepSummary: Another explanation of תוקע עצמו לדבר הלכה: a judge who rules by comparing cases on his own even though his teacher is available.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or say: 'one who pushes himself into a matter of הלכה' means a judge who gets a case, learned a ruling, compares one matter to another, and has a teacher but does not go to ask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a completely new meaning to the third phrase. It is not about Torah without doing, but about a judge who relies on himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judge knows a similar ruling and decides by comparison alone. His teacher is around, yet he does not ask. Relying on his own comparison instead of asking risks a wrong ruling, and that is what brings trouble on him.

keyTerms.meaning: Pushes himself into a matter of הלכה

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
one who pushes himself into a matter of halakha:
this is a judge who has a case come before him,
and he learned a ruling
and he compares one matter to another,
and he has a teacher
but does not go to ask.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, תּוֹקֵעַ עַצְמוֹ לִדְבַר הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation of step 9 with a different one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תוקע עצמו לדבר הלכה is a judge who decides by his own comparison instead of asking his available teacher.

steps.title: A judge must feel a sword and גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן teaches that a judge should feel a sword between his thighs and גיהנם open below him, learned from the פסוק about שלמה's bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: A judge should always see himself as if a sword lies between his thighs and גיהנם is open beneath him, as it says: 'Here is שלמה's bed, sixty mighty men around it, of the mighty men of ישראל... because of fear at night', meaning fear of גיהנם, which is like night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports step 17 by showing how much fear a judge should have. That is why he must ask his teacher and not rely on himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of warriors with swords around שלמה's bed, afraid at night. רבי יונתן reads these as judges, the sword as the danger of a wrong ruling, and the night as the darkness of גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: A sword placed between his thighs
The place of punishment after death

steps.whatToRemember: 'תוקע עצמו לדבר הלכה' gets several explanations. Through רבי יוסי's ברייתא: learning without doing is not even learning (רב פפא), or one gets no reward through others' doing. Or else it means a judge who relies on his own comparisons when his teacher can be asked, because judging is very dangerous.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:
A judge should always see himself

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ חֶרֶב מוּנַּחַת לוֹ בֵּין יְרֵיכוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: as if a sword were placed between his thighs,
and Gehinnom were open beneath him,
as it says: “Here is the bed of Shlomo,
sixty mighty men around it,
of the mighty men of Israel, etc.
phrases.notes: The skipped words include 'each man has his sword on his thigh', which is the source for the sword image.

phrases.english: because of fear at night”,
meaning fear of Gehinnom,
which is like night.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 17 by showing the great danger a judge faces.
steps.raayaObject: That a judge who rules alone without asking his teacher brings trouble on himself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יונתן's teaching based on שיר השירים 3:7–8.

steps.title: Quoting רבן גמליאל's opinion from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of רבן גמליאל's ruling in the משנה to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: If she refuses, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the opening words of רבן גמליאל's opinion from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case: a man is married to a minor girl, and her adult sister falls to him as a יבמה. רבן גמליאל says that if the minor does מיאון, the יבמה can do יבום. If not, they wait until the minor grows up, and then the יבמה goes free because she is his wife's sister.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor girl's refusal, which ends a marriage that exists only by rabbinic law
A girl under the age of adulthood
A widow waiting for יבום with her late husband's brother
A wife's sister, who is forbidden to the husband

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
If she refuses, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of his words in the משנה: if not, she waits until the minor grows up, and then the יבמה goes free as a wife's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אִם מֵיאֲנָה וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the minor does not refuse, the יבמה waits until the minor grows up and then goes free as a wife's sister.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks רב for רבן גמליאל's reason, with two possible options
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks רב whether רבן גמליאל's reason is that a minor's קידושין become full on their own when she grows up, or that betrothing a יבמה's sister releases the יבמה once relations take place after the minor grows up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked רב: What is רבן גמליאל's reason? Is it because he holds that a minor's betrothal hangs in suspense, and when she grows up it grows up with her, even if he did not have relations with her? Or perhaps it is because he holds that if a man betroths his יבמה's sister, the יבמה is released and goes free. If he had relations with her after she grew up, then yes; if he did not, then no?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks רב why, according to רבן גמליאל, the יבמה goes free once the minor grows up. He offers two possible reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: a minor's קידושין 'hang', so the moment she grows up they become full Torah-level קידושין on their own, even without relations. Option two: רבן גמליאל holds that betrothing the יבמה's sister releases the יבמה, even though the יבום bond came first. But the marriage only becomes full when he has relations with the girl after she grows up. The practical difference is whether relations after adulthood are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question, not an attack)
They hang in suspense; not yet final
They grow up with her, becoming complete when she becomes an adult
Or perhaps; it introduces the second option

steps.confusionAlert: Both options lead to the same ruling, that the יבמה goes free. The question is only about why, and whether relations after the minor grows up are needed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked Rav:
What is Rabban Gamliel's reason?
Is it because he holds
that a minor's betrothal hangs in suspense,
and when she grows up, it grows up with her,
even though he did not have relations with her?
phrases.notes: He means relations after she became an adult.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is because he holds:
one who betroths the sister of his יבמה,
the יבמה is released and goes free,
so if he had relations with her, yes,
and if he did not have relations, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מֵרַב: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling quoted in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבן גמליאל's ruling rests on a minor's קידושין becoming full on their own at adulthood, or on releasing the יבמה through a marriage completed by relations after adulthood.

steps.title: רב answers: the reason is that betrothing the יבמה's sister releases her, but only once relations take place
steps.stepSummary: רב says רבן גמליאל's reason is the second option: betrothing the יבמה's sister releases the יבמה, but only if he had relations with the sister after she grew up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: This is רבן גמליאל's reason. It is because he holds that if a man betroths his יבמה's sister, the יבמה is released and goes free. If he had relations, yes; if he did not have relations, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב chooses the second option from רבי אלעזר's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the minor's קידושין do not become complete on their own when she grows up. The יבמה goes free only after the husband has relations with the sister once she is an adult. Before that, the יבמה is not released.

keyTerms.meaning: She is released and goes free (no יבום and no חליצה)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: He said to him: This is Rabban Gamliel's reason,
because he holds:
one who betroths the sister of his יבמה,
the יבמה is released and goes free,
so if he had relations, yes,
and if he did not have relations, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's question by picking the second option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן גמליאל holds that betrothing the יבמה's sister releases the יבמה, and here that happens only after relations once the minor has grown up.

steps.title: רב ששת says רב must have said this while half-asleep
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת sharply challenges רב's answer, saying רב must have said it while dozing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: I say that רב said this teaching while he was dozing and lying down.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks רב's answer, saying it is so hard to accept that רב must not have been fully awake. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying someone spoke 'while dozing' is a strong way of saying the statement is mistaken. רב ששת is about to show that a known ברייתא contradicts רב's view that relations after adulthood are needed.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: I say
that while Rav was dozing and lying down,
he said this teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אָמֵינָא, כִּי נָיֵים וְשָׁכֵיב רַב, אֲמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's answer from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the יבמה goes free only after relations with the grown-up sister.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's explanation goes against an accepted source, so רב ששת says it could only have been said carelessly.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that a minor's betrothal becomes complete when she grows up
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings a ברייתא saying a minor's קידושין are 'suspended'. He explains that this must mean they become complete on their own when she grows up, even without relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: One who betroths a minor girl, her betrothal is suspended. What does 'suspended' mean? Is it not that when she grows up, it grows up with her, even though he did not have relations with her?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת backs up his challenge with a ברייתא about a minor's קידושין. He reads it as matching the first option, which רב rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls a minor's קידושין 'suspended'. רב ששת argues that the only sensible meaning is that they become full on their own when she grows up, with no relations needed. If so, there is no need for רב's explanation, which requires relations after adulthood.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Is it not...? It introduces the expected obvious answer

steps.whatToRemember: רב says the יבמה goes free only after relations with the grown-up sister. רב ששת uses the ברייתא of 'suspended' קידושין to argue that a minor's קידושין become complete on their own when she grows up.

phrases.english: As it is taught: One who betroths a minor girl,
her betrothal is suspended.
What does 'suspended' mean?
Is it not that when she grows up, it grows up with her,
even though he did not have relations with her?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת הַקְּטַנָּה — קִידּוּשֶׁיהָ תְּלוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind רב ששת's challenge in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That a minor's קידושין become complete on their own when she grows up, even without relations, against רב's explanation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת הַקְּטַנָּה — קִידּוּשֶׁיהָ תְּלוּיִין.

steps.title: רבין explains 'suspended' as depending on relations
steps.stepSummary: רבין בריה דרב נחמן rejects רב ששת's proof. He says the 'suspended' קידושין of a קטנה stay undecided until the husband has relations with her as an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בריה דרב נחמן said to him: This matter of the minor girl really is 'suspended.' If he has relations with her after she grows up, yes, her קידושין are complete. If he does not, no, they are not. This is because she says to herself: 'He has an advantage over me, and I have an advantage over him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבין defends רב by showing that the ברייתא רב ששת quoted can be read another way. In his reading, 'suspended' means 'waiting on relations after she grows up.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת read 'suspended' as 'waiting until she grows up, then complete automatically.' רבין reads it as 'waiting until he has relations with her as an adult.' The reason is that each side can still walk away: he can divorce her, and she can refuse him. So she never fully commits until there are relations once she is an adult, and the ברייתא no longer contradicts רב.

keyTerms.meaning: It stays hanging in suspension, not yet decided either way
He had marital relations with her
He has an advantage over me
I have an advantage over him

steps.confusionAlert: Both רב ששת and רבין agree the ברייתא says 'suspended.' They only argue about what the suspension is waiting for: her growing up, or relations after she grows up.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִין בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Ravin, son of Rav Nachman, said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב ששת, who just brought the ברייתא against רב.

phrases.english: This matter of the minor girl
really does stay in suspension,
if he has relations with her, yes, the קידושין are complete;
if he does not have relations with her, no, they are not.
For she says: He has an advantage over me,
phrases.notes: His advantage is that he can divorce her. Her advantage is that she can refuse him while she is still a minor.

phrases.english: and I have an advantage over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִין בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects רב ששת's proof from the ברייתא by reading 'suspended' differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects רב ששת's reading of the ברייתא. It does not reject the ברייתא itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Suspended' does not have to mean 'automatically complete at adulthood.' It can mean 'waiting on relations after she grows up.'

steps.title: רב's own ruling seems to contradict this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב really requires relations. In his מחלוקת with שמואל, רב says a קטנה who grew up without refusing and then married someone else needs no גט from the second man.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב really hold: if he had relations, yes; if not, no? But it was stated: A minor girl who did not refuse, grew up, and then went and married someone else. רב said: She does not need a גט from the second man. שמואל said: She does need a גט from the second man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's answer, as defended by רבין, using a different ruling that רב himself gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case, nothing is said about the first husband having relations with her after she grew up. Even so, רב says the second marriage means nothing, so she needs no גט from the second man. That suggests רב holds her first קידושין became complete on their own once she grew up, which is the opposite of what he told רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he really hold? This opens a challenge.
It was stated: an argument between אמוראים is being quoted
She refused: a minor walking away from her marriage
She grew up and reached adulthood

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a contradiction inside רב's own opinions. The גמרא will now have to resolve it.

phrases.english: And does Rav really hold:

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּעַל — אִין, אִי לָא בְּעַל — לָא?
phrases.english: if he had relations, yes; if he did not, no?
But wasn't it stated:
A minor girl who did not refuse her husband,
and grew up, and then went and married someone else,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה גֵּט מִשֵּׁנִי,
phrases.english: Rav said: She does not need a bill of divorce from the second man,
and Shmuel said: She does need a bill of divorce from the second man.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַב אִי בְּעַל אִין אִי לָא בְּעַל לָא וְהָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבין defends רב, the גמרא attacks the same position from another ruling of רב's.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that a קטנה's קידושין become complete only after relations once she is an adult (step 21, as explained in step 24).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules that a grown-up קטנה needs no גט from a second husband, even though no relations as an adult are mentioned. That implies her first קידושין completed automatically, which contradicts his requirement of relations.
